# PLTR (Palantir Technologies Inc., NMS) Technical Report, as of 2026-10-28

## 1. Indicator selection (8, with rationale)

| Role | Indicator | Why it is included |
|---|---|---|
| Long-term trend | `close_200_sma` | Strategic trend filter |
| Medium-term trend | `close_50_sma` | Dynamic trend and pullback reference |
| Short-term trend | `close_10_ema` | Fast read on momentum shifts |
| Momentum/trend change | `macd` | Crossover and divergence. The snapshot also supplies its signal line and histogram, so I did not request those separately. |
| Overbought/oversold | `rsi` | Shows the October overbought run and the reset since |
| Volatility/range | `boll` | The 20-period basis. The snapshot supplies the upper and lower bands. |
| Risk sizing | `atr` | Stop distance and position sizing |
| Volume-confirmed trend | `vwma` | Shows whether volume supports the price trend |

This set avoids redundancy. It has three moving averages at different horizons, one momentum oscillator, one trend-momentum tool, one volatility range, one risk measure and one volume-weighted measure.

## 2. Data integrity note

The snapshot and `get_indicators` agree on every overlapping value: 10 EMA 197.33, 50 SMA 186.28, 200 SMA 153.45, RSI 53.87, Bollinger middle 197.16, MACD 3.63 and ATR 7.68. The snapshot's histogram of -1.03 matches MACD minus signal (3.63 - 4.65), allowing for rounding.

VWMA (199.15) comes only from `get_indicators` and is not in the snapshot, so it is not independently verified. The latest-day volume (20,375,259) is a non-round figure. I can't tell from the tool output whether the 2026-10-28 session is complete, so treat that day's volume and close as potentially provisional.

## 3. Verified snapshot (2026-10-28)

- **OHLC:** open 197.01, high 198.72, low 193.13, close 196.81.
- **Volume:** 20,375,259.
- **Bollinger:** lower 183.86, middle 197.16, upper 210.46.
- **MACD:** line 3.63, signal 4.65, histogram -1.03.
- **ATR:** 7.68.

## 4. Trend structure

**Long-term and medium-term trend are firmly up.**
- The close of 196.81 is about 28% above the 200 SMA (153.45) and about 5.7% above the 50 SMA (186.28).
- The 50 SMA is well above the 200 SMA, by about 33 points, so the golden-cross configuration is in place. The data does not show when the cross occurred, so this is an established alignment, not a fresh signal.
- Both averages are rising:
  - The 50 SMA climbed from 165.03 on 09-28 to 186.28 on 10-28.
  - The 200 SMA rose slowly from 152.05 to 153.45.
- Price context from the data: the closing low in the six-month window was 107.27 on 06-25. The highest close was 209.05 on 10-09, and the highest intraday high was 212.94 on 10-12.

**Short-term trend is neutral and consolidating.**
- Price is marginally below the 10 EMA (197.33) and the Bollinger middle (197.16). It is further below the VWMA (199.15), by about 2.3 points.
- The 10 EMA has been flat, between 195.85 and 197.44 since 10-16, which fits sideways chop.
- Since the 10-09 peak, closes have ranged from 186.03 (10-16) to 209.05 (10-09). The last eight closes sit between 192.60 and 201.72.

## 5. Momentum

**MACD: positive but decaying.**
- The line peaked at 8.39 on 10-13 and has fallen on most sessions to 3.63. It is still above zero, so the larger trend is intact.
- It is below its signal line (4.65), with a histogram of -1.03. That is a bearish crossover state, indicating momentum is cooling, not reversing.
- A MACD line that turns up and recrosses its signal would be the first sign that the consolidation is resolving upward.

**RSI: reset from overbought to neutral.**
- RSI reached 76.29 on 10-09, 76.20 on 10-12 and 75.61 on 10-13, all above the 70 threshold.
- It fell to 46.27 on 10-16, the day of the sharp selloff, then recovered to the 52–59 range. It is 53.87 today, down from 56.09 on 10-26.
- This is neither overbought nor oversold and leaves room in both directions. The overbought condition has already cleared, so the stretched-momentum risk from mid-October is mostly gone.
- The 10-16 reading of 46.27 is the weakest in the window. RSI did not break lower on the 10-19 to 10-28 retests.

## 6. Volatility and range

- The Bollinger bands are 183.86 / 197.16 / 210.46, so the width is about 26.6 points, or about 13.5% of the middle band.
- Price sits near the middle, so there is no band-based overbought or oversold signal.
- The middle band has risen steadily from 178.46 (09-28) to 197.16 (10-28), confirming the uptrend over the 20-day basis.
- ATR is 7.68, about 3.9% of price. It rose from about 6.0–6.7 in early October to a peak of 8.23 on 10-21–10-22, and is easing again (7.84 on 10-27, 7.68 on 10-28). That points to mildly contracting volatility after the October swings.
- The 10-16 session shows the current volatility regime:
  - High 203.55, low 184.45, close 186.03, versus the prior close of 200.50 (a fall of about 7.2%).
  - Volume was 33.35M.
  - The next session (10-19) closed at 194.15, and 10-21 closed at 201.72.

## 7. Volume confirmation

- The 10-08 and 10-09 breakout came on higher volume (41.9M and 37.6M), against the typical 15–25M in late September and October. The close moved from 194.12 on 10-07 to 209.05 on 10-09.
- Volume on the pullback days was moderate (24.3M on 10-14, 24.8M on 10-15, 33.4M on 10-16). The 10-16 selloff was on above-average volume for the period, which was a warning sign.
- Recent sessions have low volume (15.1M–22.9M from 10-20 through 10-28, with 10-28 possibly incomplete), consistent with consolidation, not conviction.
- VWMA (199.15) is above the simple price averages, which means heavier volume has traded at higher prices. This is mostly the 10-08 to 10-09 breakout. Price sitting below VWMA means recent volume-weighted buyers are marginally underwater, a mild short-term headwind.
- For historical context, the 08-04 earnings-style gap (close 125.65 on 08-03 to 162.66 on 08-04, on 175.0M volume) was the largest volume event in the six-month window. I can't attribute a cause from the tool data.

## 8. Actionable levels (reference only)

These are levels derived from indicators and prior highs and lows in the data. I am not claiming any of them has held as support or resistance in the past.

| 212.94 | Window high (10-12) |

| ~201.7 | 10-21 close, top of the recent closing range |
| 199.15 | VWMA |

| 186.03 | 10-16 close (lowest close of the October retest) |
| 184.45 | 10-16 low |

**ATR-based risk sizing.**
- With ATR at 7.68, a 1.5x ATR stop is about 11.5 points below entry, about 185.3 from the current close.
- A 2x ATR stop is about 15.4 points, about 181.4.
- The 1.5x level sits close to the 50 SMA (186.28) and just above the 10-16 low. The 2x level is below the lower band.
- Because ATR is about 3.9% of price, position sizes should be scaled for daily moves of roughly ±$7–8.

## 9. Scenarios

**Bullish continuation.**
- It would be supported by a close back above the 10 EMA and VWMA (about 197–199), then above ~201.7.
- The MACD histogram would turn positive, and RSI would move back above about 60 while volume rises.
- The first upside references are the upper band (210.46) and the 209.05 closing high, then the 212.94 window high.

**Bearish/corrective.**
- It would be signaled by closes below the 10-16 low (184.45) and the lower band (183.86), which would also take price below the 50 SMA (186.28).
- MACD would turn negative and RSI would move below the 46.27 level of 10-16.
- That would mean a deeper pullback within the larger uptrend. The 200 SMA at 153.45 is far below and is not an immediate reference.

**Base case.** Continued range-bound consolidation between about 184–202 while momentum resets. The tools support a "trend up, short-term neutral, momentum cooling" description, not a decisive entry signal.
